title: Generate strict task proposals at the host boundary

requirement.summary: Let a host Coding Agent convert one ordinary-language work request into the existing strict low-risk task-proposal and read-only admission preview without sending raw conversation to AgentGov Core or admitting the task automatically.

objective.rationale: Core already validates normalized proposals and preserves human-only admission, while the selected next product gap is the host-owned conversion from an ordinary request into that contract.

goal: Add a replaceable host materializer seam that produces a strict proposal and existing admission plan, proves raw-request non-retention and denied authority with fixtures, and leaves final ADMIT handling unchanged.
non_goals: Do not add a model, credential, network call, host installation, or production semantic materializer.
Do not send raw prompt, transcript, source content, credentials, or absolute host paths to AgentGov Core or place them in the normalized proposal and rendered preview.
Do not let the materializer generate authority, admit a task, write a repository, start a session, or bypass the existing exact human confirmation.
Do not modify NYC, add another host, commit, push, publish, release, or deploy.
acceptance_signals: One ordinary-language request invokes a replaceable host materializer exactly once and yields the existing strict task-proposal and read-only admission-plan contracts.
The Adapter, not the materializer, supplies proposal identity, source actor, privacy declarations, and denied authority before existing Core validation.
Raw request text is absent from the proposal, admission plan, result evidence, and bounded failure output; AgentGov reports zero model and network calls.
Malformed or unsafe normalized drafts fail before repository mutation, and corrected retry can use a fresh Adapter invocation.
The existing interactive ADMIT path remains the only write boundary and is covered end to end with a deterministic fixture materializer.
Documentation distinguishes the implemented host contract seam from an unimplemented production semantic materializer or live host integration.

items: A semantic materializer may omit or distort the user's intent, so its output must remain a non-authoritative proposal for human review.
An over-broad result or exception could retain raw conversation or host-local data.
Existing uncommitted Adapter 1.2.4 files share the working copy and must be preserved without being misrepresented as part of this feature.

stop_conditions: Stop if implementation requires raw conversation to enter Core, persist in Adapter results, or appear in failure diagnostics.
Stop if the materializer can admit a task, write files, start work, or grant code, scope, Git, release, deployment, or external authority.
Stop if completion requires a model, credential, external service, host installation, or another live replay.

decision.rationale: The product owner selected option 1, automatic proposal generation, as the next bounded requirement on 2026-08-07.
